page: Microsoft Azure F8als_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Falsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at a base frequency of 3.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU tests placing the instance in the top 10% tier and Geekbench single-core scores ranking in the top 25%. Text processing performance is also highly competitive, reaching the top 10% tier. However, multi-core performance across stress-ng and Geekbench tests falls into the average category. A notable hardware tradeoff is the memory subsystem; while cached small-block read bandwidth is average, the uncached large-block read bandwidth is weak, placing in the bottom 25% tier.

Given the dedicated CPU allocation, high clock speed, and low memory density, the F8als_v6 is designed for compute-bound workloads that do not require large memory footprints. The qualitative cost profile reflects a high compute-to-memory ratio, making it resource-efficient for CPU-intensive tasks such as compilation, text processing, and light LLM inference, where it achieves strong text generation speeds on small models. It is less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale data analytics due to the 16.0 GB memory limit and weak uncached memory bandwidth.
